notes:
Summary: ApexShield is a regulated regtech vendor building a compliance automation suite that will ingest sensitive regulatory PDFs and customer-submitted evidence. They want a private VPC deployment with strict data residency (EU for EU customers, NA for US customers), BYOK KMS integration, and audit-grade logging. Primary regulatory drivers: SOC 2 + ISO 27001 as baseline, HIPAA (for a small subset of customers handling PHI) and PCI considerations for workflows that may touch payment tokens.

Customer asks / mapping (requested during security deep-dive):
- SOC 2: they want to map Redwood Private controls to common SOC 2 CC categories. Top asks: evidence of logical access controls (SSO/SAML + SCIM), encryption in transit and at rest (integrated with customer KMS), separation of control/data plane for tenant isolation, audit log delivery and retention options (7 years requested), and recent SOC 2 Type II report.
- ISO 27001: interested in mapping to Annex A controls: A.9 (access control), A.10 (cryptography - KMS/BYOK), A.12 (ops security - logging/monitoring), A.13 (communications security - VPC peering, private endpoints), and A.18 (compliance). Requested ISO certificate copy and statement on continuous improvement/ISMS scope when Redwood Private is deployed in a VPC.
- HIPAA / BAA: they will require a BAA for segments that process PHI. Key asks: ability to sign a BAA, clear data flow diagram for PHI through Redwood runtime (are prompts persisted to logs?), options to disable prompt logging or scrub PHI, and encryption keys managed by customer (BYOK) with key rotation policies. Also asked for H:ealthcare penetration test and vulnerability disclosure process.
- PCI considerations: not full cardholder data processing in LLM prompts is their preference. For any cases touching tokens, they want guidance on scope reduction (segmentation), examples of prompt redaction and tokenization, and confirmation that audit logs will not contain PANs. They asked for a short playbook for developers to avoid PCI scope creep.

Redwood feature mapping (what our team walked through):
- Private VPC deployment: control plane options (private control plane), customer VPC peering, NAT/egress rules, and optional on-prem connector. Good fit for their isolation/residency needs.
- KMS integration: BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) with envelope encryption; customer asked for HSM-backed options and evidence for key separation.
- Audit logging & retention: configurable forwarding to customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and S3 with retention policy; logs include request metadata and system events. We recommended suppression of sensitive fields in payloads and demonstrated log scrubbing hooks.
- Access & identity: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning; RBAC for routes/models; support for MFA enforced via IdP.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II report available under NDA, ISO27001 certificate available for validated control scope, pen test summary provided.

POC scope proposed: 4-week technical POC in customer dev VPC -> deploy Redwood Private control plane in private mode, test BYOK integration (customer AWS KMS), verify log forwarding to customer Splunk, run a simulated PHI ingestion scenario with logging disabled/scrubbed, and validate EU residency for a sub-project. Deliverables: runbook, network diagram, short compliance mapping spreadsheet (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/PCI) and a security findings remediation plan.

Quotes / paraphrases from security lead: "We need clear answers on what data leaves our VPC, how keys are used, and an auditable chain for every request. If Redwood can give BYOK + 7y logs into our S3 + BAA, procurement will move fast."

Next steps (technical + legal):
- Finalize POC SOW and sign mutual NDA + BAA (legal).
- Confirm KMS BYOK workflow and any HSM proof artifacts (crypto team).
- Provide SOC2 Type II redacted report and ISO27001 certificate under NDA (compliance).
- Deliver developer playbook for PCI avoidance and log-scrubbing guidelines (solutions engineering).
